
# EventFlow — Project Knowledge Hub

> Official public knowledge base for the EventFlow project.
> Last updated: 2026-11-11.
> Language: Russian.
> Documentation status: actively being assembled.

## Project

EventFlow is a digital invitation and event management service.

This repository contains publicly available project context, product documentation, architecture summaries, historical audit registry, database documentation, and agreed decisions.

It is a public knowledge hub. The complete working documentation remains in a separate private repository.

## Start Here

Read these documents in the following order:

1. [AI_CONTEXT.md](AI_CONTEXT.md) — overall project context, product principles, architecture, and development history.
2. [AI_HANDOFF.md](AI_HANDOFF.md) — instructions for continuing work without losing context or repeating completed tasks.
3. [PROJECT_STATUS.md](PROJECT_STATUS.md) — current verified status and open tasks.

## Product Documentation

- [Product Overview](01_product/README.md) — purpose, users, functionality, commercial model.
- [Architecture Overview](02_architecture/README.md) — components, data model, access control, backend principles.
- [Decisions Registry](05_decisions/README.md) — agreed decisions, preliminary decisions, and open questions.

## Technical Documentation

- [Audit Registry](03_audits/README.md) — historical audits and rules for checking their relevance.
- [Database Documentation](04_database/README.md) — database architecture and safe SQL usage.
- [Initial SQL Archive](04_database/initial/README.md) — description and restrictions of historical SQL materials.

## Project History

- [Changelog](06_changelog/README.md) — significant project and documentation changes.

## Important Rules for AI Agents

- Read AI_CONTEXT.md, AI_HANDOFF.md, and PROJECT_STATUS.md before starting work.
- Inspect relevant existing documentation before proposing another audit.
- Do not repeat completed audits without a specific reason.
- Do not treat historical SQL files as the current production schema.
- Never run the initial SQL archive blindly against the active database.
- Distinguish verified facts, agreed decisions, preliminary decisions, hypotheses, and open questions.
- Do not claim that a feature is implemented merely because it is described in product documentation.
- Do not change agreed architectural or commercial decisions without discussing the change.
- Update relevant documentation after significant project changes.
- Do not publish secrets, credentials, tokens, private customer data, or other confidential information.

## Documentation Limitations

This hub is being populated progressively.

The presence of a document does not necessarily mean that the described functionality has been implemented or recently verified.

For the latest confirmed state, consult PROJECT_STATUS.md and check the actual application and database when necessary.
